title: Quantitative mass spectrometry of HAX1 WT and HAX1 KO promyelocytic cells reveal differences in amino acid synthesis and lipid metabolism
projectDescription: part of a project: Granulocyte differentiation arrest in HAX1-deficient cells demonstrated in a new in vitro model of Kostmann disease, is caused by ineffective lipid droplet autophagy and fatty acids uptake. Molecular and metabolic mechanisms underlying congenital neutropenia in patients with HAX1 deficiency are not clear at the moment. It was demonstrated that HAX1 deficiency results in the arrest of neutrophil differentiation. Our studies of the effect of HAX1 deficiency on proteomic and metabolic profiles of promyelocytic cells have led to a conclusion that HAX1-deficient cells display differences in amino acid metabolism, specifically arginine, serine and aspartate. The analysis revealed significant upregulation of several proteins in HAX1-deficient cells, specifically argininosuccinate synthase (ASS1), an enzyme of arginine biosynthesis pathway, with the highest upregulation score, confirmed by Western blot. Moreover, Quantitative System Metabolism (QSM) analysis of the proteomic data has led to a conclusion, supported by specific tests, that fatty acid metabolism is affected in HAX1-deficient cells.  This assumption was confirmed by experiments showing that the lipid droplet content is increased in HAX1-deficient cells, pointing to the accumulation of fatty acids that are not metabolized. Studies of autophagosome formation and function in HAX1 WT and knockout (KO) cells revealed that autophagy of lipid droplets is defective at the stage of the fusion with the lysosome. It is known that autophagy-dependent generation of free fatty acids is critical for neutrophil differentiation, therefore if HAX1 deficiency affects normal autophagy of lipids in promyeloblasts it should explain its effect on differentiation arrest.
sampleProcessingProtocol: HL-60 and HL-60 HAX1 knock-out cell lines were grown in RPMI1640 medium with L-glutamine (Biowest) and 10% Fetal Bovine Serum (Gibco) at 37 °C in a 5% CO2. Four separate cultures were prepared for each cell line. 8x106 cells were collected from each sample. Next,samples were prepared according to FASP protocol with minor modifications. Peptide concentrations were measured using Pierce Quantitative Colorimetric Peptide Assay (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA). Before trypsin digestion, cysteine were reduced with 10mM TCEP and blocked by 5 min incubation at room temperature with 30 mM s-methylmethanethiosulfonate (MMTS). Digestion was carried out overnight using 3 µg of trypsin (Promega GmbH, Mannheim, Germany) at 37 o C. Peptide concentrations were measured using Pierce Quantitative Colorimetric Peptide Assay (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA). 90 µg of each sample in 30 µl was labelled with iTRAQ 8plex (SCIEX, Framingham, MA, USA) tags in 140 ul isopropanol for 2 hour on vortex. The reaction was quenched by the addition of 8µL 5% hydroxylamine. combined iTRAQ sample was desalted using three 30 mg Oasis HLB cartridges (Waters, Milford, MA, USA). Aliquots were dried and resuspended in 500 µl 10 mM ammonium hydroxide. Sample was fractionated for 25 fraction using high-pH reverse-phase chromatography on XBridge Peptide BEH C18 column (4.6 x 250 mm, 130 Å, 5 µm, Waters). Separation was performed at 0.8 ml/min flow rate for 27 minutes on Waters Acquity UPLC H-class system. Mobile phases consisted of water (A), acetonitrile (B) and 100 mM ammonium hydroxide solution (C). 25 fractions were dried in Speedvac and reconstituted in 0.1% formic acid in water (Evosep solvent A) by 15 min sonication and 15 min vortexing.  Fractions were analysed using LC-MS system composed of Evosep One (Evosep Biosystems, Odense, Denmark) directly coupled to a Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany). 20 µl (one tenth) of peptides from each fraction was loaded onto disposable Evotips C18 trap columns (Evosep Biosystems, Odense, Denmark) according to manufacturer protocol. Chromatography was carried out at a flow rate 500 nl/min using the 44 min (30 samples per day) preformed gradient on EV1106 analytical column (Dr Maisch C18 AQ, 1.9 µm beads, 150 µm ID, 15 cm long, Evosep Biosystems, Odense, Denmark). Data was acquired in positive mode with a data-dependent method using the following parameters. MS1 resolution was set at 60 000 with a normalized AGC target 300%, Auto maximum inject time and a scan range of 300 to 1700 m/z. For MS2, resolution was set at 15 000 with a Standard normalized AGC target, Auto maximum inject time and top 40 precursors within an isolation window of 1.4 m/z considered for MS/MS analysis. Dynamic exclusion was set at 20 s with allowed mass tolerance of ±10 ppm, the precursor intensity threshold at 5e3 and Precursor Fit threshold at 70%. Precursor were fragmented in HCD mode with normalized collision energy of 32%. Spray voltage was set to 2.1 kV, funnel RF level at 40, and heated capillary temperature at 275 °C.
dataProcessingProtocol: Offline recalibration, as well as peptides and proteins identification, was performed in the MaxQuant/Andromeda software suite (version 1.6.17.0) [2] using Homo sapiens a full Uniprot database (version 20210426). The search included tryptic-generated peptides, Metylthio (C) was set as a fixed modification and Oxidation (M) as a variable one. Reporter MS2 quantification was specified in order to obtain values for quantitative analysis. Reverse database was used for target/decoy statistical results validation, peptide and protein FDR was set to 0.01. Also match between runs function was enabled.  Protein groups along with quantitative data were further analysed in Perseus (version 1.6.14.0) [3]. Hits from reversed database and proteins only identified by site. Proteins with less than 3 samples in each groups were filtered out. iTRAQ reporter values were normalized on average sum of intensity [4]. Reporter intensities were log2 transformed, missing values were replaced with data from normal distribution (width 0.3, down shift 1.8) separately for each column and PCA analysis, as well as Volcano Plot, were performed. Subsequently, two-sample t-tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR were performed to compare expression changes between groups. Significance threshold for resulting q-value was 0.05.
